cases.sentence: Но противно тому, что неизменно совершалось во всех ___, вместо ожидаемого известия о бегстве неприятеля, стройные массы войск возвращались оттуда расстроенными, испуганными толпами.
cases.explain: «прежних сражениях» — after the preposition «во», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Napoleon’s generals—Davout, Ney, and Murat, who were near that region of fire and sometimes even entered it—repeatedly led into it huge masses of well-ordered troops. But contrary to what had always happened in their former battles, instead of the news they expected of the enemy’s flight, these orderly masses returned thence as disorganized and terrified mobs. The generals reformed them, but their numbers constantly decreased. In the middle of the day Murat sent his adjutant to Napoleon to demand reinforcements.

cases.sentence: — сказал Наполеон с ___, как бы не понимая его слов, и глядя на красивого мальчика-адъютанта с длинными завитыми, черными волосами (так же, как носил волоса Мюрат).
cases.explain: «строгим удивлением» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Reinforcements?” said Napoleon in a tone of stern surprise, looking at the adjutant—a handsome lad with long black curls arranged like Murat’s own—as though he did not understand his words. “Reinforcements!” thought Napoleon to himself. “How can they need reinforcements when they already have half the army directed against a weak, unentrenched Russian wing?”

cases.sentence: ___ с длинными волосами, не отпуская руки от шляпы, тяжело вздохнув, поскакал опять туда, где убивали людей.
cases.explain: «Красивый мальчик-адъютант» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Napoleon rose and having summoned Caulaincourt and Berthier began talking to them about matters unconnected with the battle.

cases.sentence: — Не успел еще Бельяр скрыться из вида, как с ___ прискакал новый посланный с поля сражения.
cases.explain: «другой стороны» — after the preposition «с», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “You are very fiery, Belliard,” said Napoleon, when he again came up to the general. “In the heat of a battle it is easy to make a mistake. Go and have another look and then come back to me.” Before Belliard was out of sight, a messenger from another part of the battlefield galloped up.

cases.explain: «беспрестанными помехами» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.

cases.explain: «гневным жестом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: The adjutant bent his head affirmatively and began to report, but the Emperor turned from him, took a couple of steps, stopped, came back, and called Berthier. “We must give reserves,” he said, moving his arms slightly apart. “Who do you think should be sent there?” he asked of Berthier (whom he subsequently termed “that gosling I have made an eagle”).

cases.sentence: С ___ продолжали прискакивать адъютанты, и все, как бы сговорившись, говорили одно и то же.
cases.explain: «разных сторон» — after the preposition «с», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Friant’s division disappeared as the others had done into the smoke of the battlefield. From all sides adjutants continued to arrive at a gallop and as if by agreement all said the same thing. They all asked for reinforcements and all said that the Russians were holding their positions and maintaining a hellish fire under which the French army was melting away.

cases.sentence: Все просили подкреплений, все говорили, что русские держатся на своих местах и производят un feu d’enfer,[716] адский огонь, от которого тает ___.
cases.explain: «французское войско» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.

cases.explain: «складном стуле» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Napoleon sat on a campstool, wrapped in thought.

cases.sentence: ___ сожаления, раскаяния и восторга просияла на лице господина Боссе, и он плывущим шагом отошел к другим генералам.
cases.explain: «Блаженная улыбка» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Go away …” exclaimed Napoleon suddenly and morosely, and turned aside. A beatific smile of regret, repentance, and ecstasy beamed on M. de Beausset’s face and he glided away to the other generals.
